newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks end at six-week low.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks end at six-week low.

text.p: SPI futures 2218 -15 US 30yr cl 7.04 -0.01
10yrbond futs 92.020 steady Gold (NY cl) $381.10 -1.65
NIKKEI closed FTSE cl 3964.10 -10.20
*Stocks close at six week low in light trade, miners lead drop as metals prices continue to soften. Turnover 217.15 million, value A$547.10 million, 984 stocks traded, 318 steady, 224 up, 442 down

The Australian share market dived to its lowest closing level in six weeks on Monday, the resource leaders routed as the few interested investors sold out amid concerns over fragile-looking base metals prices.
At 4.10 p.m. (0610 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 21.6 points lower at 2219.20.
September share price index futures were 15 points lower at 2218, a 1.2 point discount to the underlying index.
With offshore equity markets regularly reaching record highs, local traders expressed dismay at the local market's disappointing performance and wondered where to from here.
"Very disappointing," said the director of institutional sales at James Capel, Stephen Streeter.
"We thought it (the market) had enough in the fundamentals but it has been soft. Hills (BHP) led the market down and the golds were belted after its price fell."
One broker said light turnover levels suggested most investors had preferred to stay out of the market rather than actively selling stock.
"Lots of people are waiting for the FOMC meeting in the States which means we have to wait until Wednesday for the lead," said a Sydney broker.
Streeter agreed, but added that the Australian market needed a positive result given what appeared to be downward turn in local sentiment.
"People are waiting for the FOMC but we need a decent lead from the States. If it's negative, you have to ask how far our market can come back," he said.

Takeover activity at the smaller end provided the only interest of the day. Allied Queensland Coalfields shares rose sharply as a competing bid emerged from Singapore-based Marsford Investments while oil producer Discovery Petroleum saw its shares up after an offer from British group Premier Oil.
Other features remained elusive in a what was described as a generally dull and uninspiring day's performance.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about two to one, while about 32 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures trading saw reasonable interest although options trade was at a snail's pace.
Total options traded 34,194 (50,183)
Turnover in September SPI contracts totalled 6,446 (6,766)
In other local markets, Australian bonds saw a thin session as the market awaited Tuesday's FOMC meeting where a tightening in policy is seen as a strong possibility, traders said.
Local yields were marginally lower after treading a narrow range, but turnover was restricted to just over 3,000 lots when a normal day would see over 10,000.
By 5.00 p.m. (0700 GMT), 10 year T-Bonds were yielding 7.95 percent, down 0.02 from Friday.

The Australian dollar made slight gains through a choppy session as U.S. banks turned buyers, catching a holiday-dulled market short. Traders reckoned the resilience of support was bullish but cautioned that confidence would be fragile while the currency was still short of Friday's US$0.7944 high. By 5.00 p.m. (0700 GMT), the local dollar was quoted at US$0.7924/29.
